grounding: research/correlation-psd-and-welch.md and relevant source-summary results from Stoica-Moses chs. 1-2, J. O. Smith ch. 6, Oppenheim-Schafer ch. 10/App. A, and Harris IV.A-C

study.failure: Any changed frozen number or violated scientific invariant exits nonzero; success prints one JSON report.

frozen_contract.record: N=16384, n=0,...,N-1; normalized frequency in cycles/sample; two-sided PSD per (cycles/sample)
frozen_contract.noise: circular complex white Gaussian CN(0,1): independent real and imaginary N(0,1/2); this makes the one-bin periodogram exponential and avoids DC/Nyquist exceptions
frozen_contract.raw_probe: rectangular full-record periodogram at f=0.25 for prefix lengths 256,1024,4096,16384
frozen_contract.welch_probe: periodic Hann w[n]=0.5-0.5 cos(2*pi*n/M), calibration f=0.3125, M in {32,64,128,512,2048,4096}, overlap in {0,0.5,0.75} where declared
frozen_contract.tones: x[n]=0.5 exp(j2*pi*0.18n)+0.5 exp(j2*pi*0.22n)+v[n]; separation=0.04; the resolution curve is the exact mean over all legal frame starts plus the unit noise floor
frozen_contract.resolution_rule: PASS iff two distinct local maxima are each within 0.01 cycles/sample of the true tones and the intervening valley is at least 1 dB below the lower peak; dense grid step=1/8192
frozen_contract.cv_rule: sample standard deviation divided by sample mean across the same 96 seeded trials; Welch target PASS iff CV<0.30

formulas_and_scales.wss_pair: r_xx[l]=E{x[n+l]x*[n]}, S_xx(f)=sum_l r_xx[l] exp(-j2*pi*f*l), integral_-0.5^0.5 S_xx(f)df=r_xx[0]
formulas_and_scales.cv: CV=s_sample/mean_sample; for independent circular-Gaussian periodograms CV approximately 1/sqrt(K)
formulas_and_scales.overlap: rho_h=sum_n w[n]w[n+hH]/U; K_eff=K^2/[K+2 sum_{h>=1}(K-h)|rho_h|^2]; predicted CV=1/sqrt(K_eff)
formulas_and_scales.hann_resolution: ENBW=1.5/M cycles/sample; first-null-to-first-null width=4/M cycles/sample. These are declared scales, not a universal two-tone theorem.

course_spec_reconciliation.exact_reading: With the frozen measurement rules above, M=64,128,2048 at 50% overlap all separate the 0.04-spaced tones and have empirical CV<0.30 over 96 seeded trials.
course_spec_reconciliation.frontier: M=32 meets CV but merges the tones; M=4096 separates them but misses CV. The useful target is therefore genuinely two-sided, not a guaranteed win.
course_spec_reconciliation.required_precision_repair: The current prose spec omits signal type/amplitude, PSD scaling, window convention, overlap choices, the bin at which CV is measured, and an operational definition of tone separation. Preserve the prose target but implement exactly the frozen_contract fields; otherwise PASS/FAIL is not reproducible.
course_spec_reconciliation.recommended_success_preset: M=2048, periodic Hann, 50% overlap: resolved and CV=0.267121, close enough to both boundaries to make the tradeoff visible.

acceptance: Executable reproduces every frozen CV within 5e-7 and M=64 valley depth within 5e-7, using exactly 96 trials.
Every raw N has 0.75<CV<1.25 and N=16384 CV exceeds 0.8 times N=256 CV.
Welch M=128 has CV<0.30; M=4096 has CV>0.30.
M=32 is merged; M=64 is separated; halving 64 to 32 exactly doubles Hann ENBW.
For each Welch row, empirical CV differs from overlap-corrected prediction by <0.09.
At M=512, overlapped K_eff<K; 75% overlap raises nominal K by >3.8x versus 0% but K_eff by <2.2x.
Demo D1-D5 pass, all presets match raw unrounded lookup values, and manual keyboard/light-dark/360px checks pass.
boundaries: The PSD-autocorrelation pair requires a WSS model; a finite sample average is not the ensemble expectation.
Complex analytic noise is deliberate. Real data have conjugate symmetry and special DC/Nyquist degrees of freedom, so their exact CV constants differ.
The overlap K_eff formula is exact here for circular-Gaussian one-bin powers under the declared window/frame model; it is not a universal independence correction for arbitrary signals.
CV is calibrated in a noise-only band at f=0.3125; deterministic tone bins can have much lower relative variability and must not be used to claim broadband estimator stability.
The 1 dB/tolerance peak rule is a declared demo criterion, not a universal Rayleigh limit. Unequal tones, other phases/windows, colored noise, or nonstationarity can change resolvability.
Rounded display values never decide PASS/FAIL; all assertions use full double-precision values.
